evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.44: in suīs studiīs tantōs prōgressūs … facere
terms.comment: Progress made in learning or a skill: prōgressūs facere. Latin often says it with a verb: quantum prōfēcerit, how far he has come on; crēscit, he is growing (see develop).

evidence: Sen. Ep. 11.1: quantum jam etiam prōfectūs
terms.comment: From prōficiō; in Ovid and post-Augustan prose (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 52: vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta
terms.comment: Of plants and animals growing, and of anything that increases.

phrases.latin: in quō quantum esset animī, quantum ingeniī, quantum jam etiam prōfectūs, sermō prīmus ostendit
phrases.english: our first conversation showed how much spirit and talent he had, and how far he had already come on

phrases.latin: jam tibi discipulus crēscit cicarō meus. jam quattuor partīs dīcit
phrases.english: my little lad is growing into a pupil: he can already divide by four

phrases.latin: Quid ego vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta commemorem?
phrases.english: Why should I tell of the vines’ sprouting, planting and growth?

sources: Lewis & Short: progressus · Lewis & Short: profectus · Lewis & Short: incrementum
